1.
Counter affidavit filed by the State is taken on record.

2. The State with its counter affidavit has filed a copy of the written information given to the informant of the instant case, however, despite personal service the informant is not represented before this Court.

3. Heard Shri Firoz Ahmad Khan, learned counsel for the applicant/appellant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
4.

This appeal has been preferred under Section 14 (A) (2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 against impugned order dated 30.07.2024, passed by Special Judge, (SC/ST Act), Faizabad/ Ayodhya in bail application no. 1514 of 2024 CNR No.
UPFZ01-004148/2024, (Zeeshan Vs. State of U.P.), arising out of case Crime No. 262/2024, under Zeeshan vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of ... on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3686074/
1 Sections 366, 376, 323, 506, 427, 406 IPC and Sections 3(2) (V) of SC/ST Act, Police Station- Raunahi, District Ayodhya, whereby the bail application of the appellant/applicant has been rejected.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in this case.

The FIR of the case has been lodged by the mother of the victim alleging therein that her daughter has been enticed away by the appellant on 22.5.2024 and she has also taken with her some jewellery and Rs. 20,000/- as cash and according to her daughter her age is 21 years.
6.

It is vehemently submitted that the prosecutrix/ victim herself appeared before the S.H.O. of the concerned Police Station on 27.5.2024 and had given a written application stating therein that her age is about 21 years and she was having relationship with the appellant and on 24.5.2024 had gone with the appellant to Punjab and when they got information about lodging of the FIR, she has returned.
7.

It is also highlighted that in her statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.
the prosecutrix has specifically stated that she was having an affair with the appellant and her family members have solemnized her marriage with some one against her wishes and on the relevant day she had gone to Punjab with the appellant.
8.

Highlighting above statements of the prosecutrix, it is vehemently submitted that the prosecutrix as per the own admission of the prosecution was more than 19 years at the date and time of the incident and when she has herself gone with the appellant, no offence, in fact has been committed by the appellant.
He is in jail in this case since 30.5.2025 and there is no apprehension that the accused-appellant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
9. Learned A.G.A. on the other hand opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant/ appellant.
8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears to be an admitted situation that the prosecutrix is/ was major.
She has stated to have accompanied the appellant on her own volition.

She also refused to undergo any medical examination and had appeared before the Station House Officer of the Police Station concerned herself and informed that she had gone with the appellant on her own volition and consent as she is having an affair with him and her marriage was solemnized with some one against her wishes with whom she does not want to live and she also refused to undergo medical examination.
The appellant is in jail in this case since 30.05.2024 and he is not having any criminal antecedent.

9. Thus, having regard to the above facts and circumstances of the case, in the considered opinion of this court material illegality has been committed by the trial court in rejecting the prayer of bail of the appellant.
10. In result, the appeal filed by the appellant is allowed and the order dated 30.07.2024, passed by Special Judge, (SC/ST Act), Faizabad/ Ayodhya is hereby set-aside.

sentences.text:
Let appellant-Zeeshan be enlarged on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following additional conditions, which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The appellant shall not tamper with the evidence of witnesses and shall not commit any offence.
(ii) The appellant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(iii) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through her counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) In case, the appellant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the appellant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(v) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the appellant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
12. Observations made herein-above are only for the purpose of disposal of bail application and the same shall not have any bearing on the trial of the case.
